**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

## What looks good

- The diff changes one number in one test, one comment block, and one decision file. No production code changed.
- The safety asserts of the test do not change. The rough over its own bar stays silent. The top level starts at the stock radius. The program posts. The d20 bar stays below 9,000 moves.
- The cause is real. PR #3496 removed the `seam.is_none()` guard at `crates/motion/src/machining3d/hsm.rs:145`. A seam level now calls `zigzag_ringed_passes` with a `SeamWrap`. `boundary_rings` adds a ring for each boundary loop (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_zigzag.rs:87`). The extra moves are intended.
- The new readings match. The test prints `d20 bar 7578 moves | d12.4 bar 2110 moves`. These are the values in the PR body and in the decision file.
- The decision file follows `docs/decisions/README.md`: one heading, what was decided, why, what was dropped, and the cost to change later.
- `Changelog: none` is correct. This PR changes no shipped behaviour.

## Results with main (built locally, own worktree and target)

Trial merge with `origin/main` (`3c68dcaf2`): clean.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate test a_rough_over_an_oversized_bar_peels_from_the_stock_radius --crate camcraft-app --binary rotary_verify --exact` | ok, 1 passed |
| whole `rotary_verify` binary | ok, 10 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-motion` `rotary_zigzag_rings` (the #3496 ring tests) | ok, 3 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test rotary_verify -- -D warnings` | clean |

The quick plan maps the diff to one step: `app rotary_verify (1 fn)`. That step is in the table above.

## Light lane (six steps, each run alone)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| light build (release `--no-run`) | ok, 557 s |
| motion light: lib | ok, 7 passed |
| motion light: adaptive_troch_island | ok, 1 passed |
| motion light: adaptive_troch_neck | ok, 1 passed |
| motion light: adaptive_troch_parallel | ok, 1 passed |
| app light: pocket_pass_start | ok, 1 passed |

## Targeted tests

- No post or toolpath production code changed, so the example catalog suites are not required.
- The PR is `P2`, so no targeted heavy step is required.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes

- `crates/app/tests/rotary_verify.rs:342` says "after: 7,082". The current d20 count is 7,578. That line was stale before this PR. The new lines give the current numbers. A follow-up can correct it. It does not block this merge.
- `crates/app/tests/rotary_verify.rs` is 424 lines and this PR adds five lines. Note only.
- The slow `example_catalog` failure of the post-merge run is not this test. This PR does not touch it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 473600714d1e3af9a9332bf2c9774882a956ba24 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Review tier: safety floor (rotary toolpath motion). I checked the claim against the code and the tests of #3496. I did not rely on the PR body.

### What looks good
- The cause is correct. PR #3496 (merge `6eff704f2`) removes the `seam.is_none()` guard in `machining3d::hsm::plan_level` on purpose. Its comment in `crates/motion/src/machining3d/hsm.rs` and `docs/decisions/3168-rotary-zigzag-seam-rings.md` say this. The wrap levels now take `zigzag_ringed_passes(..., Some(SeamWrap))`. That ring drops the two seam edges, so no azimuth is cut twice.
- #3496 pins that motion in `crates/motion/tests/rotary_zigzag_rings.rs`: `the_wrapped_ring_cuts_no_azimuth_twice` (no crossing feed pairs, wall scallop in reach), `the_dflat_edge_walls_are_ringed` and `the_near_end_loop_without_a_seam_vertex_keeps_its_closing_edge`.
- The new motion is not a gouge on these fixtures:
  - The d20 bar verifies with no blocking warning, starts at the stock radius and posts (`rotary_verify.rs:332-337`).
  - The d12.4 bar (the 2,110-move program) verifies silent, every rapid states its pose, `verification_report` has no problems, and it posts with G43.4 (`rotary_offset_on_a_round_bar_verifies_clean_and_posts`, `posts_clean` at `rotary_verify.rs:237-250`).
- No extra air cutting: the d20 bar, which has the air levels, went down (7,648 -> 7,578) and stays under the 9,000 bound.
- The change is one test number, one comment and a decision file. No production code changes. The decision file has the format of `docs/decisions/README.md`.
- Body: `Changelog: none` (test only), ends `Fixes #3774`, the commit subject is conventional. No process files, no snapshot PNGs, no goldens.

### Results merged with main (locally; trial merge with `origin/main` at `f6716cdcd`, clean)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (plan: `app rotary_verify`, 1 fn) | ok, 97 s |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test rotary_verify` (whole binary) | 10 passed, 0 failed. Reading: `ROTARY OFFSET \| d20 bar 7578 moves \| d12.4 bar 2110 moves` |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test rotary_verify -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo xtask gate light` (release) | 6 steps ok: motion light lib, adaptive_troch_island, adaptive_troch_neck, adaptive_troch_parallel, app light pocket_pass_start |

### Heavy lanes
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run`: the diff reaches no heavy lane. `app heavy: rotary_verify` has no `#[ignore]`d test, so it has no step. This is a P2 PR, so no targeted heavy step is owed.
- Other tests that the guard removal of #3496 can change: I searched the heavy and light tests. The only heavy tests that build a rotary Offset Zigzag/Auto program are in `crates/app/tests/rotary_field_parity.rs` (`the_offset_kind_reads_the_radial_law`, `the_offset_kinds_eye_cost_is_measured`). They assert field-to-law parity and sign misses, not a move count. They are not reached by this diff and I did not run them. They run at the cut. No light twin is rotary. No other test pins 2,064 or 7,648.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. The pin is weak. `assert_eq!(snug, 2110, ...)` (`rotary_verify.rs:351`) is a bare move count. Each correct change to the wrap ladder moves it, as #3496 did. The law that it guards is "the matching bar has no air level". I recommend a `P7` follow-up issue that pins that law directly, for example: the count of levels above the part's skin on the d12.4 bar is 0, or the d12.4 program equals the unsplit ladder's program. Then the count can go or become a loose bound.
2. The PR body says the rings "add moves on purpose". This is true for the d12.4 bar (+46). The d20 bar went down by 70. Before #3496, a seam level used `side_rings`; now it uses the ringed zigzag rows, so the count can move both ways. The bound holds, so this is only a note for the decision file.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
